key_insight: Clinical System One (CS1), a 4-billion-parameter model, makes fast, typed judgments from patient records while generalist language models formulate questions and synthesize evidence.
clinical_relevance: CS1 could support population-scale record review and clinical-trial screening, with answer probabilities helping route uncertain cases to human review.
method: Trained on 12.4 million question–answer pairs from 3.6 million patients across a multi-hospital health system.
Answers multiple typed questions in one forward pass without task-specific retraining.
Pairs with language-model agents for cited longitudinal-record answers and trial-eligibility screening.
evidence_signal: On 963,408 held-out patients, CS1 outperformed open decision models up to 27B parameters on 13 of 14 independently scored tasks; across 21 external datasets, it approached the strongest tested 27B model’s aggregate performance with 6.4× faster inference in a matched workload.
watch_item: Prospective validation and local probability calibration remain important before deployment; the abstract does not establish improved patient outcomes.
paper_title: A general-purpose System One decision model for clinical records
